description.narrative:
At the G8 summit in Gleneagles in July 2005, the G8 members proposed to supplement the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) with the Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative (MDRI) allowing for 100 percent relief of eligible multilateral debts to the World Bank, the African Development Bank and the International Monetary Fund. The purpose of both the HIPC and the MDRI is to free up resources for development and investments in the SDGs. Countries that have completed the HIPC process are eligible for multilateral debt relief under the MDRI. Along with the donor community, Denmark has committed to provide funding for the World Bank and the African Development Fund to enable these two institutions to provide debt relief. ¨
Because the debt to be cancelled was originally issued provided on highly concessional terms, maturities are very long. This implies that donors must commit to fund the provision of debt reliefs several years from now. Funding to the World Bank continues until 2044, while funding for the African Development Bank continues until 2054. Denmark renews its unconditional commitment to the MDRI every third year.

The Fund reported a surplus of UA 58.21 million in 2024, down from UA 115.27 million in 2023. The surplus fell because of an increase in administrative expenses which more than offset the higher interest income and fair value gains on treasury investments. Structural changes in the Fund include the cancellation of loans to several beneficiaries under the Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative (MDRI) and the increased share of grants in country allocations due to the deterioration of some countries’ debt sustainability analysis (DSA). These changes have not adversely affected the financial sustainability or commitment capacity of the Fund, which stood at UA 4.06 billion in 2024 (UA 4.25 billion in 2023).
To learn more about MDRI, please find the newest Annual Report 2024 (Published 27 May 2025): https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/annual-report-2024
